$comment: Hand-edited properties; geometry rebuilt from trace.json by make past (decision 12).

properties.name: Emery, by Fortieth St and San Pablo Ave, to Russell St, Berkeley

sources.note: Trains left "Emery station on arrival of the Berkeley train"; freight "received at Fortieth street and San Pablo avenue".

properties.notes: Where the line ran between Emery and Berkeley is OpenHistoricalMap's reading of the 1895 sheet, unchecked: no later sheet here shows track on it. It crosses San Pablo Ave at Fortieth St, where the sources put the depot and freight office.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200263309 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS San Francisco 1895 topographic map, cut to -122.27943,37.85491; checked on USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1899) and USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). From the Southern Pacific's Berkeley line at Emery, east beside Fortieth St, across San Pablo Ave at Fortieth St, where the line's depot was, and north to Russell St, Berkeley. Not checked: the 1899 sheet draws the line here too faintly to compare, and by 1949 no track was left on it.

properties.name: Russell St, Berkeley, by Albany to near Stege
properties.notes: The Santa Fe's Oakland line later ran on this right of way; the 1949 sheets draw its track here.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200263309 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS San Francisco 1895 topographic map, cut from -122.27943,37.85491; checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949), USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949) and USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1899). From Russell St, Berkeley, by University Ave and Albany to near Stege. The 1949 sheets draw the Santa Fe's track on this right of way, and the way follows it within a few metres; the 1899 sheet draws the line about 150-200 m further west, which is that sheet's misregistration.

properties.name: Near Stege, by San Pablo and San Pablo Creek, to Orinda Park

sources.note: Trains "to the end of the road near Orinda Park, General Wagner's ranch" in October 1889.

properties.notes: Most of the creek's valley is under San Pablo Reservoir today.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap ways 200250635, 200250636 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Concord CA 1897 topographic map; USGS San Francisco 1895 topographic map, cut to -122.20642,37.90176; checked on USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1899) and USGS Concord 1:62,500 (1897). By San Pablo and up San Pablo Creek, under today's San Pablo Reservoir, to Orinda Park. The 1897 Concord sheet labels it "California and Nevada R.R.". Orinda Park is placed 2.5 miles back from Bryant along the line, the length Poor's gives the 1891 extension; no source here locates its station.

properties.name: Orinda Park to Bryant

sources.note: "The extension from Orinda Park to Bryant was built in 1891."
The line as 20.0 miles and 2.5 miles, the second being the Bryant extension.

properties.notes: Built in 1891 (Poor's); its opening to trains isn't dated.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200250636 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Concord CA 1897 topographic map, cut from -122.20642,37.90176; checked on USGS Concord 1:62,500 (1897). Orinda Park to Bryant, the extension built in 1891, where the 1897 Concord sheet ends the line at "Bryant".
